chapter: Chicago, the Woodside, the army and 52nd Street
title: Meeting Jimmy Blanton and Floyd Smith in St. Louis and Pittsburgh
summary: In 1936 with Roy he jammed all night with Blanton and Floyd Smith, and met Blanton again in Pittsburgh and New York.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: And after Art Tatum I was with Roy Eldridge, there, and speaking of Roy Eldridge, I -- my first trip out of town I think was to St. Louis, with Roy Eldridge, where I first met Jimmy Blanton, and Floyd Smith was playing guitar with Jeter and Pillars Band.. And I had just -- and Floyd Smith and the band was -- Floyd Smith was quite a guitarist, but I want to talk about Jimmy Blanton. I --
Oh, I imagine it was around '36, around that time.
He was still in his teens,

Well, yeah, I guess so.) He was quite young. But he was playing professional. He was playing in this club, and we went there, I think it was just for one or two nights. But after -- the first night we were there after we finished the job we went by this club where Jeter and Pillars was playing, and I met Floyd and Jimmy Blanton. And --

Well, they both were just tremendous. Of course Blanton was just a virtuoso, he was just fabulous. I had never heard anything like that before, so we played all night, naturally. We jammed and played --

Jimmy Blanton and Floyd, Floyd Smith, yes. And I didn't see Blanton any more for quite a while, as I probably told you before until I joined Fletcher, and we were in Pittsburgh, and he was in Pittsburgh. He was working on this boat with Fate Marble. I forget his name, it was a St. Louis band, and they -- this boat would sail between Pittsburgh and St. Louis, and he was there. I met him on the hill, in Pittsburgh that night, we were hanging out. This was the first time we saw Evrol Gardner. And he was -- still in his home town.

Evrol yeah, was playing in some club, the Ritz I think the name of a club was. And it was very nice seeing Blanton again. The next time I saw him was in New York he had joined Duke, and I was working with Roy at this time, at Kelley's Stables. And Blanton would come and play every night, and it was just a thrill. But his death was just untimely, and I think Charlie Christian died right after that. They died around the same time, around the same age. I think they were in their early twenties. Yes.
